answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to cryptographic stake burning with superlinear cost scaling C(n) = k * n^2. An attacker cannot simply wander across multiple dummy profiles: creating each extra node requires burning non-refundable stake. Like a predatory falcon diving on fraudulent nodes, slashing contracts destroy their pigment stake upon detection, imposing exponential economic friction against mass spoofing.
